name: González-Alvarez House ('The Oldest House')

dates.altered: Wood-frame second storey added after 1774 by Major Joseph Peavett, who also glazed openings previously shuttered; a two-storey coquina wing added by Geronimo Alvarez; restored 1959-60 by the St. Augustine Historical Society to its presumed late eighteenth-century appearance (survey and Wikipedia agree on the outline).
dates.note: The Wikipedia infobox prints 'circa 1723, 1775–1786, 1790'; the survey's first documentary record of the house is a 1727 burial entry; the style node gives 1723. Nothing edited to agree.

refs.title: NRHP reference No. 70000845; added April 15, 1970; designated NHL April 15, 1970; contributing property of the St. Augustine Town Plan Historic District (ID70000847); location 14 St. Francis St. (as the Wikipedia infobox prints it)

survey.prepared: The history 'was compiled by the St. Augustine Historical Society in 1962' (as Part I says); the architectural description carries no author line in the extract; a later chronology in the same PDF cites Gjessing and Waterbury.

quotes.text: A. General Statement: 1. Architectural character: The Gonzalez-Alvarez House, one of the earliest surviving domestic structures in Spanish Florida, was restored in 1959-60 after extensive archival and archaeological research. The restoration returned the house to its presumed late eighteenth-century appearance, 2. Condition of fabric: Restored; well maintained.
quotes.page: No page marker legible in the extract span (Part II.A); the nearest marker elsewhere in the extract reads 'HABS No, FL-138 ... Page 29'.

quotes.text: B. Description of Exterior 1. Number of stories: Two stories. Over-all dimensions: Approximately 56' (five-bay front) x 32'. Rectangular shape.
quotes.page: Part II.B.1; no page marker legible in the extract span.

quotes.text: 2. Foundations: Coquina (local shellstone) blocks. 3- Wall construction: Coquina rubble; plastered inside and out. Upper story is part wood framed with clapboarding.
quotes.page: Part II.B.2-3; no page marker legible in the extract span.

quotes.text: 4. Porches: Wooden porch on east elevation, second level; covered loggia at north elevation.
quotes.page: Part II.B.4; no page marker legible in the extract span.
Part II.B.5; no page marker legible in the extract span.

quotes.text: 6. Openings: a. Doorways and doors; Unmolded wooden paneled doors of random design, and some are board and batten. b. Windows and shutters: Six-over-six-light, double- hung (upper sash fixed); one eight-over-eight-light double-hung sash, second floor; casement sash lower east elevation.
quotes.page: Part II.B.6; no page marker legible in the extract span.

quotes.text: 7. Roof: a. Shape, covering: Gable roof with wooden shingles. b. Eaves: Marrow open eaves.
quotes.page: Part II.B.7; no page marker legible in the extract span.

quotes.text: C. Description of Interior 1. Plans: Basically this two-story structure had a two- room plan; this has been extensively added to, and could be considered a variation of the "St. Augustine Plan" (rear loggia) discussed by Albert Manucy In his book, The Houses of St. Augustine (St. Augustine, Florida: St. Augustine Historical Society, 1962).
quotes.page: Part II.C.1; no page marker legible in the extract span.

The survey says the coquina ground storey carries a PART wood-framed upper storey with clapboarding, which is the node's own description; it also records a gable roof of wooden shingles and narrow open eaves, which the node's prose about the borderlands (flat azoteas or 3:12-5:12 tile) does not cover for the Florida branch.
